description:
PagePilot is an e-book reader built for iPhone, iPad, and Mac that lets you turn pages hands-free using your Apple Watch.

CORE FEATURES

▸ Apple Watch Page Control
Read on iPhone or iPad / Mac, then flick your wrist or press the Digital Crown to go to the next page. No touching the screen required — perfect for reading in bed, during meals, or on the go.

▸ OPDS Feeds
Add OPDS feeds to browse and download books from public libraries and publishers — expand your library beyond local files.

▸ Multiple Formats
Supports EPUB, PDF, Audiobooks, and CBZ comics. One app for your entire library.

▸ WiFi Transfer
Open a URL on your computer's browser, drag files in, and they appear in your library instantly. No cable, no iCloud required.

▸ Device Transfer
Send books directly between your iPhone and iPad / Mac over the same Wi-Fi network.

▸ Reading Stats
Track your daily and weekly reading time, monitor your progress, and maintain a reading streak.

▸ Library Management
Browse a cover grid, filter by reading status, and sort by recent import, recent read, title, or author. Multi-select and bulk delete.

▸ Text-to-Speech (TTS)
Full system voice support with adjustable speed and pitch.

▸ Daily Reading Goal
Set a daily reading goal in minutes and track your progress from the home screen.

WHY PAGEPILOT?

PagePilot was built for one reason: poking at your screen to turn a page shouldn't be the friction point in your reading experience. Whether you're standing on the subway, lying in bed, or on a treadmill, Watch page control makes reading feel more natural.

PagePilot Pro unlocks unlimited books (free version holds up to 10), unlimited highlights & notes (free version keeps up to 20), weekly/monthly/yearly reading stats, streak tracking, and the ability to use Apple Watch on iPad / Mac.

PagePilot keeps these features free forever: basic Watch page turning, WiFi transfer, and device-to-device transfer — because these are the prerequisites for getting value from PagePilot.

whatsNew:
Read on Mac in a dedicated reading window, with your bookshelf close at hand.

• Browse a cover grid and filter books by reading, unread, or finished.
• Open books in separate windows. Reopening the same book brings its existing window forward.
• Turn EPUB and PDF pages with the mouse wheel, trackpad gestures, or the previous and next buttons.
• Use keyboard shortcuts for page turning, the table of contents, search, and reading settings. Press Escape to close panels.
• Keep reading controls and the page indicator clear of the text as you resize the window.

Continuous scrolling remains available, and zoomed PDF pages keep their native panning behavior.
